# PM-MKSSY Aquaculture Insurance: Bridging India's 1% Fish Cover Gap


As India targets a resilient Blue Economy, PM-MKSSY replaces open-ended subsidies with parametric digital tools to secure smallholder aqua-farmers.

India's aquaculture sector sustains over 30 million livelihoods but has historically operated with under 1% insurance penetration.


### Overview


India's aquaculture sector is expanding rapidly, yet risk protection has lagged behind. The Union Cabinet approved the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana as a Central Sector sub-scheme under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana. The policy targets **digital formalisation** and direct premium subsidies to fix this gap.


Insurance penetration has stalled **below 1%** across water spread areas. Severe disease volatility and steep premiums have kept private underwriters away.


Rather than adopting open-ended crop subsidies, PM-MKSSY introduces a **one-time premium incentive** tied to the National Fisheries Digital Platform. Farm-level verification and landholding caps protect vulnerable smallholders while laying down baseline actuarial data.


## Why in the News: Launch of the Aquaculture Insurance Framework Under PM-MKSSY


The Union Cabinet approved the **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY)** on 8 February 2024 as a dedicated Central Sector sub-scheme under the broader **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)** framework.


The four-year programme runs from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27 with a **total outlay of ₹6,000 crore** . Key operational pillars include:


- **Blended Financing Model:** Public funding makes up 50% (₹3,000 crore), financed partly through multilateral borrowings from the **World Bank** and the **Agence Française de Développement (AFD)** .
- **Private Co-Investment:** The remaining 50% (₹3,000 crore) is structured from anticipated private beneficiary contributions and commercial equity.
- **Formalisation Mandate:** The scheme establishes an **institutional shift toward formalisation** , securing credit and risk transfer for a sector sustaining **over 30 million livelihoods** .

## The Risk Trap: Why India's Aquaculture Insurance Penetration Stalled Below 1%


Aquaculture insurance penetration in India has historically **stalled below 1%** of total cultivated water spread area, leaving millions of primary producers exposed to sudden economic collapse.


Production, however, continues to climb. India achieved a record fish production of **19.8 million tonnes in 2024-25** , with the inland and aquaculture sector contributing over 74% (14.74 million tonnes). Average aquaculture productivity reached **4.77 tonnes per hectare** , approaching the national benchmark of 5 tonnes per hectare.


Sector Metric Performance Figure


**Total Fish Production (2024-25)** 19.8 million tonnes


**Inland & Aquaculture Share** >74% (14.74 million tonnes)


**Average Pond Productivity** 4.77 tonnes/ha (Target: 5.0 tonnes/ha)


**Dependent Population** Over 30 million livelihoods


**Historical Insurance Penetration** Below 1% of water area


Despite these gains, commercial insurers have stayed away due to unsustainable loss ratios. Private underwriters quoted **prohibitive premium rates** between 8% and 15% of the total sum insured, pricing out small-scale fishers.


Biological pathogens drive these loss ratios. Research by ICAR-CIBA indicates that epidemics like **White Spot Syndrome Virus (WSSV)** , *Enterocytozoon hepatopenaei* (EHP), and infectious myonecrosis can wipe out shrimp crops within 48 hours. Compounded by coastal cyclones, these biosecurity threats drove insurers out of the market.


The aquaculture risk cycle illustrates how severe viral epidemics like WSSV drive prohibitive premium rates and underwriter market exit.

## Understanding PM-MKSSY: Architecture, Premium Subsidies, and Eligibility Rules


Component 1-B of PM-MKSSY establishes a targeted **one-time premium incentive** to encourage formal insurance adoption across the aquaculture sector.


Under Component 1-B, general category fish farmers receive an incentive of **40% of the insurance premium cost** . This is capped at ₹25,000 per hectare for holdings up to 4 hectares, with an overall ceiling of ₹1,00,000 per farmer. The 4-hectare limit prevents **fiscal capture by large corporate entities** , steering subsidies to smallholders.


Equity provisions grant an **additional 10% premium incentive** (50% total subsidy) to Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), and women beneficiaries. The operational guidelines mandate covering at least **1,00,000 hectares of aquaculture farms** under structured insurance.


Farm / Enterprise Category Water Spread / Volume Ceiling General Category Incentive Rate SC / ST / Women Incentive Rate Maximum Incentive Cap


**Pond Aquaculture (Component 1-B)** Up to 4 Hectares 40% of Premium Cost 50% of Premium Cost ₹25,000/ha (Max ₹1,00,000 per farmer)


**Intensive Systems (RAS, Biofloc, Cages)** Up to 1,800 m³ 40% of Premium Cost 50% of Premium Cost ₹1,00,000 per unit


**Microenterprise Grants (Component 3)** Safety & Quality Upgrades 25% of Total Investment 35% of Total Investment ₹35 Lakh (Gen) / ₹45 Lakh (SC/ST/Women)


Intensive closed systems receive dedicated risk support under the scheme. Setups like **Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS)** , Biofloc, open cages, and raceways qualify for a 40% premium incentive capped at ₹1,00,000 for units up to 1,800 cubic metres.


Component 3 offers performance grants to fisheries microenterprises for cold chains and quality upgrades. General category units receive grants up to **25% of investment (capped at ₹35 lakh)** , while SC, ST, and women-owned microenterprises receive up to **35% (capped at ₹45 lakh)** .


## Claims and Assessment: How Aquatic Loss Evaluation Differs from Land Crops


Aquatic loss assessment faces distinct **physical and biological verification barriers** absent in terrestrial crop insurance.


Terrestrial crop surveyors rely on the **Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI)** to measure canopy health and photosynthetic activity from orbit. Aquaculture biomass stays submerged in turbid pond water. Consequently, optical satellites cannot measure stock density or disease damage directly.


Assessment Dimension Terrestrial Crops (PMFBY) Aquaculture Systems (PM-MKSSY)


**Visibility of Stock** Surface canopy visible to satellite optical sensors Biomass submerged in turbid pond water


**Primary Remote Sensing Tool** Satellite-derived vegetation index (NDVI) Optical satellite sensors rendered ineffective


**Disaster Decay Rate** Crop stands degrade over days to weeks Stock decomposes or sinks within hours


**Assessment Solution** Crop cutting experiments and spectral imagery Parametric proxy triggers and digital pond sensors


Rapid biological decay complicates loss adjustment. When viral outbreaks strike, mortality occurs underwater within hours. Dead stock decomposes or sinks before an external surveyor can conduct physical sampling. These constraints historically generated **acute information asymmetry and moral hazard** , causing underwriters to reject claims or exit the sector.


Unlike terrestrial crop damage, which is measurable via satellite NDVI canopy analysis, submerged biomass loss demands ground-level sensor diagnostics.

## Learning from PMFBY: Can PM-MKSSY Avoid the Pitfalls of Crop Insurance?


The structural framework of PM-MKSSY departs from the **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)** to avoid chronic fiscal burdens and insurer exits.


PMFBY relies on an open-ended premium subsidy model. Farmers pay a **statutory flat premium** (1.5% for Rabi, 2% for Kharif, and 5% for commercial horticultural crops), with the Centre and States sharing the remaining actuarial cost 50:50. In contrast, PM-MKSSY uses a **one-time Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) incentive** model to seed the market without creating indefinite state liabilities.


Structural Feature Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) PM-MKSSY Aquaculture Insurance


**Administrative Scope** Agricultural crops and commercial horticulture Inland, brackishwater, and marine aquaculture


**Subsidy Mechanism** Continuous, open-ended premium cost sharing between Centre and States One-time catalytic DBT monetary incentive paid directly to farmers


**Farmer Contribution** Uniformly capped at 1.5% to 5.0% of Sum Insured Market-determined premium minus 40% to 50% one-time subsidy


**Loss Verification Method** Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) and satellite NDVI indices Parametric physical triggers and NFDP-verified pond diagnostics


**Farm Size Eligibility** Universal coverage across all holding sizes Strict 4-hectare ceiling to curb large corporate subsidy capture


**Institutional Anchor** State Agriculture Departments and designated insurance clusters Department of Fisheries via National Fisheries Digital Platform


By avoiding **state-level subsidy settlement delays** that hampered PMFBY, PM-MKSSY preserves operational liquidity through direct central DBT transfers. Its explicit 4-hectare ceiling prevents public funds from subsidising capital-intensive commercial shrimp farms, preserving support for marginal growers.


## Structural Bottlenecks: Moral Hazard, High Actuarial Risk, and Data Deficits


Underwriting aquaculture risk requires overcoming **severe systemic bottlenecks** created by disease contagion and historical data deficits.


Primary operational and structural challenges include:


- **Spatial Contagion Across Pond Clusters:** Adjacent coastal ponds often share tidal creek intake and drainage canals. Unsterilised discharge from one farm causes **instantaneous cross-infection** across clusters, wiping out multiple holdings at once.
- **Actuarial Data Deficits:** India lacks long-term, georeferenced disease registries and historical loss records, forcing insurers to build high safety buffers into **elevated commercial premium quotes** .
- **Smallholder Exclusion and Information Gaps:** Small-scale fishers often lack formal water lease deeds or registration papers, barring them from institutional products and **locking them into informal debt traps** .
- **Lack of Specialised Loss Adjusters:** The insurance sector lacks trained fisheries biologists and pathologists to verify causes of death, triggering **prolonged claim settlement disputes** .


Parametric index insurance automates claim payouts when environmental metrics like dissolved oxygen or wind speeds breach critical thresholds.

## Way Forward: Parametric Triggers and Digital Platforms for the Blue Economy


Closing India's aquaculture protection gap requires expanding **parametric index-based insurance products** linked to digital identity infrastructure.


Parametric models settle claims automatically against **pre-agreed objective environmental thresholds** instead of post-disaster field sampling. World Bank technical reviews show that tracking proxy metrics—such as dissolved oxygen drops, tidal surges, and sustained wind speeds—enables **instant, dispute-free claim settlements** .


1. **Real-Time Data Collection:** Continuous monitoring via on-farm IoT water probes and coastal weather stations tracking dissolved oxygen, salinity, temperature, and wind speeds.
2. **Automated Threshold Breach:** Payouts trigger automatically when parameters cross pre-set limits, such as dissolved oxygen falling below 3.0 mg/L or wind speeds exceeding 80 km/h.
3. **Direct Payout Disbursal:** Funds transfer directly to enrolled bank accounts through the NFDP DBT gateway, bypassing post-loss physical surveys and avoiding moral hazard.


The Department of Fisheries launched the **National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP)** on 11 September 2024 to establish a central registry for all fisheries interventions. As of September 2026, the NFDP dashboard recorded **over 37 lakh registrations** covering fishers, fish farmers, and coastal microenterprises.


Integrating the NFDP Credit Facilitation module lets farmers submit **verified digital production profiles** directly to commercial and Regional Rural Banks, expediting credit under the **Kisan Credit Card (KCC)** scheme.


To curb disease spread, PM-MKSSY encourages clustering under **Fish Farmers Producer Organisations (FFPOs)** following uniform **Better Management Practices (BMPs)** and biosecurity standards. Combining parametric triggers, digital verification via NFDP, and clustered biosecurity creates a viable underwriting foundation for India's Blue Economy.


## Key Takeaways


- **Policy Architecture:** The Union Cabinet approved PM-MKSSY on 8 February 2024 with a ₹6,000 crore outlay (50% public funding via World Bank/AFD, 50% private equity) as a Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY.
- **Targeted Premium Subsidies:** Component 1-B delivers a 40% premium incentive capped at ₹25,000 per hectare for general farmers (maximum ₹1,00,000 per farmer up to 4 hectares), expanding to 50% for SC, ST, and women aqua-culturists.
- **Penetration Deficit:** Commercial aquaculture insurance penetration historically stalled below 1% due to high premium rates (8% to 15%) driven by extreme pathogen risks like White Spot Syndrome Virus (WSSV).
- **Assessment Differences:** Submerged biomass precludes optical satellite indices (NDVI) used in PMFBY, demanding a shift toward objective parametric triggers (dissolved oxygen levels, cyclone metrics) to eliminate moral hazard.
- **Digital Backbone:** As of September 2026, the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) has registered over 37 lakh fisheries stakeholders, connecting dynamic digital identities to insurance DBT and Kisan Credit Card facilities.
